uncited: This method is a parallel processing scheme for volume rendering where a host node handles I/O and data preparation, while slave nodes handle the computationally intensive fitting and polygon generation.
*   **Communication Buffers:** Two buffers are used for asynchronous message passing.
*   **Message Packing:** The host packs a couple of rows of subcubes into one transmission packet.
*   **Time Complexity:** The host performs I/O and C3 data computation, which is relatively fast compared to polygon generation.
The slaves perform the heavy computation.
The asynchronous nature overlaps communication with computation, reducing total time.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires local memory on slaves to store polygons until a threshold is reached.
For (3,3,3) approximation, communication time becomes less important compared to computation time.
Reduces communication overhead through message packing and asynchronous transfer.
*   **When to use:** When communication overhead is significant and the host can be utilized for data preparation and background communication management.
*   **When not to use:** When the implementation complexity is prohibitive or when the communication latency is negligible compared to computation time.
It was developed to alleviate problems associated with the host-slave partition in parallel volume rendering, specifically idle time and communication overhead.
The approach uses an interrupt handler to manage background subcube transmission, allowing the host to remain productive while waiting for slaves.
